classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that opposing motion closes the gap at the sum of the speeds, then use distance divided by closing speed to find the meeting time.

inlines.text: Two cars travel toward each other on a 100 km straight stretch of road.
They leave at opposite ends of the road at the same time.
The cars’ speeds are 100 km/h and 80 km/h.
How long does it take for the cars to pass each other?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 23 diagram below the prompt, toward the left.
spec.description: Horizontal road with marked endpoints, a centred 100 km label below, and opposing car arrows above. The Car 2 arrow is higher than the Car 1 arrow.
spec.mathematics: The cars start at opposite endpoints of a 100 km road and approach each other at 100 km/h and 80 km/h.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram labels and arrows are permanent givens; no meeting time or closing speed is supplied.

answer.worked:
Using relative velocity, Car 1 approaches Car 2 at the sum of their speeds.
$$\begin{align*}
s&=100+80\\
s&=180\text{ km/h}\\
t&=\frac{d}{s}\\
t&=\frac{100\text{ km}}{180\text{ km/h}}\\
t&=\frac{5}{9}\text{ h}
\end{align*}$$
Convert to minutes and seconds:
$$\begin{align*}
t&=\frac{5}{9}\times60\text{ min}\\
t&=33\frac{1}{3}\text{ min}\\
t&=33\text{ min }20\text{ s}
\end{align*}$$
